content: Oral hygiene refers to the practice of maintaining cleanliness of the mouth and teeth to prevent dental issues and bad breath. Teeth cleaning involves the removal of dental plaque and tartar from the teeth to prevent cavities, gingivitis, and gum disease. Gum disease is a significant cause of adult tooth loss, accounting for at least one-third of cases. Dentists recommend professional teeth cleaning at least twice a year. Professional cleaning typically includes tooth scaling, tooth polishing, and, in cases of excessive tartar buildup, debridement. This process is often followed by a fluoride treatment. However, maintaining good oral hygiene between professional cleanings is crucial to prevent tartar buildup, which can lead to the aforementioned problems. This is achieved through regular and thorough brushing with a toothbrush and the use of dental floss, which helps to prevent the accumulation of plaque-producing bacteria on the teeth. Massaging the gums is generally recommended as part of good oral health practices. Certain foods that support muscle and bone health also benefit teeth and gums. Dairy products provide vitamin D, which strengthens teeth. Lean meats, fish, and poultry supply magnesium and zinc, which are essential for dental health. Some individuals advocate brushing teeth after every meal and before bedtime, as well as flossing at least once daily, preferably at night before sleep. For some, flossing after every meal may also be recommended. Certain foods may offer protective effects against cavities. Milk and cheese, for example, can raise pH levels in the mouth, reducing tooth exposure to acid. These foods are also rich in calcium and phosphate, which may promote remineralization of the teeth. All foods stimulate saliva production, and saliva contains buffering chemicals that help stabilize the pH in the mouth at slightly above 7. Foods high in fiber may also enhance saliva flow. Sugars are strongly associated with dental cavities. Starchy foods, such as potato chips, can also harm teeth, though to a lesser extent, as starch is not an ideal food source for bacteria and must first be converted by enzymes in saliva. Sucrose (table sugar) is most commonly linked to cavities, but glucose and maltose are equally likely to contribute to tooth decay. The frequency of sugar consumption is more critical than the quantity consumed at one time. Frequent intake of sugary foods and drinks increases the duration during which teeth are exposed to low pH levels, leading to demineralization. Therefore, it is important to limit the frequency of sugar consumption to allow teeth time to repair themselves. Restricting sugary foods and drinks to mealtimes is one effective way to reduce the risk of cavities. Artificially refined sugar is not the only type that promotes dental cavities. Natural sugars found in fresh fruits and fruit juices can also contribute to tooth decay. Additionally, these foods (e.g., oranges, lemons, limes, apples) contain acids that lower the pH in the mouth. Soft drinks, even sugar-free ones, are less healthy for teeth than milk due to their lower pH and lack of calcium. Consuming sugared soft drinks throughout the day significantly increases the risk of dental cavities. The stickiness of foods also affects the risk of cavities. Sticky foods or sweets can adhere to the teeth, prolonging the time the pH in the mouth remains low, especially if they are sugary. It is essential to clean teeth at least twice a day, preferably using a toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste, to remove any food particles stuck to the teeth. Regular brushing and flossing also help remove dental plaque from the tooth surface. Smoking and chewing tobacco are associated with numerous dental health risks. Regular vomiting, as seen in individuals with bulimia, also causes significant damage to the teeth. Mouthwash or mouth rinse can improve oral hygiene. Some dental gums claim to enhance dental health. Retainers can be cleaned using mouthwash or denture cleaning solutions. Dentists may recommend dental braces to optimize oral hygiene and health. Dentures, retainers, and other dental appliances must be kept meticulously clean. This includes regular brushing and, in some cases, soaking them in a cleansing solution.
